replaced.from: Signature outfit: a plain blue Victorian child's dress with a white pinafore apron, white stockings and buckled shoes.

corrections.reason: Owner correction for evaluation: Carroll never describes Alice's dress, and the drafted light-blue dress with a plain white pinafore is the 1951 film's costume, which the suite baseline's scorers read as Disney's Alice. The replacement follows the palette of the coloured 1890 Nursery edition (yellow frock, frilled white pinafore, striped stockings). Hair, face, build and quotes are unchanged; all other records are unchanged.

payload.name: Alice
payload.note: The single protagonist of the book, the young girl who falls down the rabbit-hole and appears in every division; all entries refer to her, and her sister on the bank is not part of this cluster.

stages.label: Alice
stages.text: Alice: a young Victorian English girl of about seven, slight and small-boned, who grows very tall and shrinks very small over the course of her adventures. Skin fair with a light sunburn; long straight light-brown hair that often falls loose into her eyes, which she tosses back with a little shake of her head; bright, eager, curious features. Signature outfit: a pale yellow Victorian child's frock with short puffed sleeves and a sky-blue sash, a white pinafore with frilled shoulder straps, blue-and-white striped stockings and black strap shoes. Carries no props of her own.

quotes.quote: that queer little toss of her head to keep back the wandering hair that _would_ always get into her eyes
Curiouser and curiouser!

payload.name: Alice's sister
payload.note: Alice's unnamed older sister who sits on the riverbank with her, reads a book, and later dreams of Wonderland; both entries are the same individual, so keep them in one cluster.

stages.label: Alice's sister
stages.text: Alice's sister: an older Victorian English young woman, mature but youthful, slender build, fair skin with a faint summer flush, long light-brown hair pinned up loosely with some strands falling about her face, gentle, thoughtful expression. Signature outfit: a pale muslin summer dress with a modest high neckline and long sleeves, in soft cream with a faint sprigged pattern of blue. Signature prop: a small bound book she holds closed in her lap.

quotes.quote: sitting by her sister on the bank
the tiny hands were clasped upon her knee
she sat on, with closed eyes

payload.name: White Rabbit (the Rabbit who runs down the hole)
aliases: the White Rabbit with pink eyes
payload.note: The talking white rabbit with pink eyes and a waistcoat-pocket watch who leads Alice down the rabbit-hole and is seen hurrying along the passage; the first appearance, so the 'hurrying with a watch' figure.

stages.label: White Rabbit
stages.text: White Rabbit: an adult white rabbit of slender, nervous build, standing upright on hind legs with human posture. Fur pure white, soft and neat. Eyes pink. Ears long and upright. Dressed in a Victorian waistcoat, buttoned, with a pocket holding a small gold pocket watch on a chain. Carries the watch in hand. Mid-Victorian gentleman's attire, with a waistcoat-pocket watch as the signature prop.

quotes.quote: a White Rabbit with pink eyes ran close by her
took a watch out of its waistcoat-pocket
hurrying down it

payload.name: Dinah
payload.note: Alice's pet cat at home, mentioned only in talk and thought, never physically present; all four entries describe this same cat and should be one cluster.

payload.name: The riverbank
payload.note: The grassy riverbank where Alice sits beside her sister at the start and where the Rabbit runs past; both entries describe this same bank, so they are one place.

stages.label: The riverbank
stages.text: The riverbank: a broad, gently sloping bank of thick summer grass beside a slow river, with a flat open field stretching behind it. A tall, untidy hedge borders the field, and at its base a large rabbit-hole opens in the earth. Old trees stand nearby, shedding dead leaves onto the grass, and a still pool with tall reeds lies close by. Pale, hazy Victorian English countryside under a hot, drowsy sky.

quotes.quote: sitting by her sister on the bank
ran across the field after it
pop down a large rabbit-hole under the hedge
lying on the bank
the pool rippling to the waving of the reeds

payload.name: The rabbit-hole
aliases: the large rabbit-hole under the hedge
payload.note: A deep tunnel under the hedge that dips into a long, deep well lined with cupboards and shelves. Units 3-10.

stages.label: The rabbit-hole
stages.text: The rabbit-hole: a deep earthen tunnel under a hedge that runs straight for a stretch, then dips suddenly into a very deep well. The well's sides are lined with cupboards, book-shelves, maps and pictures hung on pegs, and a jar labelled ORANGE MARMALADE sits on one shelf. Dry roots and earth frame the shaft, ending in a heap of sticks and dry leaves at the bottom. No people are present.

quotes.quote: The rabbit-hole went straight on like a tunnel for some way, and then dipped suddenly down
it was labelled “ORANGE MARMALADE”
thump! thump! down she came upon a heap of sticks and dry leaves

payload.name: The long low hall
payload.note: The single long low hall with locked doors, lamps and a glass table where Alice shrinks and grows; the same hall recurs across divisions, including the later return through the tree-door.

stages.label: The long low hall
stages.text: The long low hall: a long, low passage-hall with a low ceiling from which a row of lamps hangs, lit warmly. Doors line both walls, all locked, with one low curtain concealing a small door about fifteen inches high. Near the middle stands a small three-legged table of solid glass with a slippery surface. Plain panelled walls and a polished stone floor. No people.

quotes.quote: a long, low hall, which was lit up by a row of lamps hanging from the roof
There were doors all round the hall, but they were all locked
a little three-legged table, all made of solid glass
a low curtain she had not noticed before, and behind it was a little door about fifteen inches high

payload.name: The little door to the garden
aliases: The little door and passage to the garden
payload.note: The small fifteen-inch door in the hall and the passage behind it leading to the garden, reached with the little golden key; the same door is called the garden door and the little golden key door in the later section, so it is one place with both entries.

stages.label: The little door to the garden
stages.text: The little door to the garden: a small door about fifteen inches high, set low in the wall of a long dim hall behind a drawn curtain, with a tiny lock for a little golden key. Beyond it a narrow passage, not much larger than a rat-hole, opens onto a lovely garden of bright flowerbeds and cool fountains. The wood is aged and plain, the frame modest, in a Victorian dream setting.

quotes.quote: behind it was a little door about fifteen inches high
it led into a small passage, not much larger than a rat-hole
a low curtain she had not noticed before

payload.name: White Rabbit (the Rabbit dressed for the Duchess who flees at the pool)
payload.note: The hurrying rabbit in a splendid waistcoat, dressed for the Duchess, who drops his gloves and fan and flees when Alice speaks to him near the pool of tears; the one who loses his gloves and fan, not the one who sends the bill.

stages.label: Dressed for the Duchess
stages.text: White Rabbit: an adult anthropomorphic white rabbit with a slim, quick build and white fur, drawn as an animal with human posture and dress. Pink-edged ears and small pink eyes. Signature outfit: a splendid Victorian waistcoat with a fine watch-chain, in rich colours, worn with a neat coat. Signature props he carries alone: a pair of white kid gloves and a large fan.

quotes.quote: It was the White Rabbit returning, splendidly dressed
with a pair of white kid gloves in one hand and a large fan in the other

payload.name: the Mouse (pool of tears)
payload.note: The mouse that fell into the pool of tears, swims with Alice, offended by talk of cats and dogs, and later tells its history on the shore; distinguish from the caucus-race Mouse by its swimming in the pool and the tale of its history.

stages.label: The Mouse (pool of tears)
stages.text: The Mouse: a small grey mouse of middle-aged bearing, with a slender body, a long thin tail, small bright eyes and a pale, pointed face, drawn with human posture and dress. Its build is slight and wet-furred after swimming. Its signature outfit is a small Victorian waistcoat and neckcloth in muted grey and brown. Signature props: none carried.

quotes.quote: it was only a mouse that had slipped in like herself
The Mouse looked at her rather inquisitively, and seemed to her to wink with one of its little eyes
who was trembling down to the end of his tail
its face was quite pale (with passion, Alice thought)

payload.name: Ada
payload.note: A girl of Alice's age whom Alice considers as a possible identity in unit 10; not present.

payload.name: Mabel
payload.note: A girl of Alice's age whom Alice considers as a possible identity in units 10 and 13; not present.

payload.name: the Duck
payload.note: A duck of the Pool of Tears crowd who swims to shore with the party, and the duck in the Caucus-Race who questions the Mouse; both are the same bird in the same gathering, so they form one cluster.

stages.label: the Duck
stages.text: The Duck: an adult domestic duck, full-bodied with a broad flat bill, webbed feet and smooth wet plumage of mottled brown and white, shown upright with human posture and dress: a Victorian waistcoat and a small hat, colours of dull olive and cream. Carries no props of its own.

quotes.quote: there were a Duck and a Dodo, a Lory and an Eaglet
"Found _what_?" said the Duck.
"it's generally a frog or a worm.

payload.name: the Dodo
payload.note: The dodo bird who proposes the Caucus-race, runs it, awards the prizes and presents Alice's thimble; the same dodo appears among the birds swimming to shore from the pool of tears.

stages.label: Dodo, main
stages.text: The Dodo: an elderly, portly bird standing upright on two stout legs, with human posture and a grave, self-important bearing. Plumage is dove-grey and brownish, the feathers draggled and wet from the pool; a large, heavy hooked beak, small round eyes, and a bald-looking pale patch on the crown. Wears a dark waistcoat and a faded, slightly rumpled Victorian gentleman's coat and a battered tall hat. Signature prop: a pair of round spectacles perched on the beak, and a short walking stick carried alone.

quotes.quote: there were a Duck and a Dodo, a Lory and an Eaglet
said the Dodo solemnly, rising to its feet
the birds with draggled feathers

payload.name: the Lory
payload.note: A bird (a Lory) who swims in the pool of tears, argues with Alice about age, and laments the Mouse leaving; both entries describe the same bird, so they are one individual.

stages.label: The Lory
stages.text: The Lory: a grown parrot-like bird of the lory kind, with a slender body, a short tail and a strong curved beak, its plumage bright and vivid when dry but draggled and clinging when wet. It stands upright with human-like posture and wears a small Victorian waistcoat and neckcloth in muted colours. It carries no props.

quotes.quote: a Lory and an Eaglet, and several other curious creatures
the birds with draggled feathers
I am older than you, and must know better

payload.name: the Eaglet
payload.note: A young eaglet among the birds and animals in the pool and caucus-race scenes; both entries are the same bird, so one cluster.

stages.label: The Eaglet
stages.text: The Eaglet: a young eagle standing upright on two legs with human posture, a fledgling of modest size with fine brown-grey down along its head and a smaller pale-feathered breast, a sharp hooked beak and bright, keen eyes. Its signature outfit is a small Victorian waistcoat of dark green wool with brass buttons and a neat, stiff collar. Its signature prop is a small folded paper spectacle case.

quotes.quote: there were a Duck and a Dodo, a Lory and an Eaglet
Speak English!” said the Eaglet.

payload.name: Pool creatures
aliases: the birds and animals that had fallen into it
payload.note: The crowd of birds and animals that fell into the pool and swim together to the shore in unit 26.

stages.label: Pool creatures
stages.text: Pool creatures: a crowd of drenched birds and small animals of varied kinds, such as a duck, a dodo, a lory and an eaglet, drawn as animals with human posture and dress. Each is wet and bedraggled, feathers and fur clinging to the body, with a small waistcoat or shawl and a little hat or bonnet where suited. Their faces are sharp-beaked or muzzled and their bodies are mostly feathered or furred in muted, soaked tones of grey, brown, white and russet.

quotes.quote: the birds and animals that had fallen into it
there were a Duck and a Dodo, a Lory and an Eaglet, and several other curious creatures

payload.name: The Duchess (named only, the Rabbit's destination)
payload.note: The Duchess the White Rabbit is hurrying to, named only and not present in this division; a mention with no scene of her own, so kept apart from the characters who appear on the page.

payload.name: Pool of Tears
aliases: the pool of tears which she had wept
payload.note: The lake of Alice's own tears in the hall, about four inches deep, where the Mouse and birds swim; distinct from the shore where the party dries off.

stages.label: Pool of Tears
stages.text: Pool of Tears: a shallow lake of salt water, about four inches deep at its edge and deepening enough to swim in, spreading across the floor of a long low-ceilinged hall of stone, its surface pooled round a tiny golden-keyed door and dim garden light beyond. The water is the spilled tears of a girl, salty and still, with no shore visible at its centre. Smooth flagstones rim the pool, with a few damp clumps of grass and pale reeds at the far edge, and a small rounded shore of sand where the swimmers reach land.

quotes.quote: a large pool all round her, about four inches deep and reaching half down the hall
she was up to her chin in salt water
the pool of tears which she had wept when she was nine feet high
the pool was getting quite crowded with the birds and animals that had fallen into it

payload.name: Shore
payload.note: The shore of the pool to which Alice leads the swimming party in unit 26.

stages.label: Shore
stages.text: Shore: the grassy bank at the edge of the pool of tears, a gentle slope of short green turf and pebbled sand meeting the salty water, with a few low reeds and tufted grasses along the margin, and a scattering of small rounded stones. Beyond the bank the land rises into an English riverside landscape, with a clump of trees and a low wooden fence line in the distance.

quotes.quote: Let us get to the shore, and then I'll tell you my history
the whole party swam to the shore.

payload.name: the Mouse (caucus-race)
payload.note: The authoritative mouse at the gathering on the bank, lectures on English history, tells the long tale about Fury and the mouse, and storms off; distinguish from the pool-of-tears Mouse by its role as authority of the caucus-race gathering.

stages.label: Mouse (caucus-race)
stages.text: The Mouse: a small grey field mouse with a notably long thin tail, standing upright on its hind legs in human posture. Adult, sleek fur clinging damp to its body, a narrow pointed snout, round dark eyes and small round ears. It wears a dark waistcoat with a neat cravat and a small dark hat; its fur is grey-brown with a paler belly and its tail is long, slender and pink-grey.

quotes.quote: the Mouse, who seemed to be a person of authority among them
looking down with wonder at the Mouse’s tail

payload.name: the old Magpie
payload.note: An old magpie who wraps itself up and leaves after Alice mentions cats.

stages.label: the old Magpie
stages.text: the old Magpie: an elderly magpie drawn as an animal with human posture and dress, standing upright; aged, rounded body; glossy black and white plumage with a long black tail; small beady eye; a dignified old-fashioned Victorian shawl or wrap of muted dark colours wound carefully about its body; a worn bonnet-free head with a sharp beak; no props carried alone.

quotes.quote: one old Magpie began wrapping itself up very carefully
the night-air doesn't suit my throat

payload.name: the Canary
payload.note: A canary who calls its children away to bed after Alice mentions cats.

stages.label: the Canary
stages.text: the Canary: a small adult songbird standing upright in human posture, middle-aged, slight and round-bodied. Its plumage is soft canary yellow with lighter yellow on the breast and darker olive-yellow on the wings and back. Its beak is short, pale and conical, its eyes small and bright. It wears a neat Victorian waistcoat in dull olive-green over a white shirt, with a small dark bow tie, and a little dark brown bonnet. It carries no props.

quotes.quote: a Canary called out in a trembling voice to its children
Come away, my dears! It's high time you were all in bed!

payload.name: the old Crab
payload.note: The mother crab who lectures her daughter about temper in A Caucus-Race and a Long Tale; not to be confused with the Classics master crab, who was a teacher recalled in The Mock Turtle's Story.

stages.label: the old Crab
stages.text: the old Crab: an elderly mother crab, rounded red-brown shell, two large claws raised in a lecturing manner, eight small legs, small eyes on stalks, a faded lavender shawl draped over her shell and a plain grey bonnet tied under her claws, a pair of wire spectacles perched on her nose, aged and matronly in bearing.

quotes.quote: an old Crab took the opportunity of saying to her daughter

payload.name: the young Crab
payload.note: A young crab, daughter of the old Crab, who snaps back at her mother.

stages.label: the young Crab
stages.text: the young Crab: a young crab, smaller and slighter than an adult, drawn as an animal with human posture and dress, standing upright on two legs with two large claws held at the sides, a small shell carapace, bright jointed legs and eyes on stalks, dressed in a neat Victorian bonnet and a little dark shawl or pinafore in muted colours.

quotes.quote: said the young Crab, a little snappishly
Hold your tongue, Ma!

payload.name: the assembled birds and animals
payload.note: The wet gathering on the bank who sit in a ring, race, and chorus their requests as one body.

stages.label: Dripping party on the bank
stages.text: the assembled birds and animals: a wet, mixed company of birds with draggled feathers and animals with fur clinging close, all dripping and cross, drawn as animals with human posture and Victorian dress such as waistcoats, hats and shawls. Their look is adult, varied in size and kind, including a Dodo, a Lory, a Duck, an Eaglet, a Mouse, a Crab and a Magpie, with plumage and fur darkened and sodden by water.

quotes.quote: the birds with draggled feathers, the animals with their fur clinging close to them, and all dripping wet
They all sat down at once, in a large ring, with the Mouse in the middle.

payload.name: The bank of the pool of tears
aliases: the bank of the pool of tears
payload.note: The shore of the pool of tears where the wet party assembles, dries off, races and talks; not the riverbank beside Alice's sister.

stages.label: The bank of the pool of tears
stages.text: The bank of the pool of tears: a wet, sodden grassy shore beside a wide pool of salt water left by Alice's tears, the ground soggy and puddled. A cleared open ring of trodden turf serves as a race-course, with a few tufts of reeds and low dripping banks at the water's edge. Scattered rushes and wet mossy stones line the shore, with the pool glistening beyond under a dreamlike Victorian-English sky.

quotes.quote: They were indeed a queer-looking party that assembled on the bank
First it marked out a race-course, in a sort of circle

payload.name: White Rabbit (the anxious householder who sends Bill and Pat)
payload.note: The anxious white rabbit who owns the house, sends Alice for gloves and a fan, and sends Pat and Bill to deal with her; the one with a house and servants, not the roadside runner or the court herald.

stages.label: White Rabbit
stages.text: White Rabbit: an anxious white rabbit in human form, slim and upright on two feet, with white fur, long ears and whiskers. Human dress: a Victorian waistcoat and coat, a pocket-watch chain, white kid gloves and a fan carried for his household. Fussy, nervous manner; a proud householder's bearing. Signature outfit: a dark-green or grey Victorian waistcoat and coat with a watch chain, colours muted and tidy. Signature props alone: a fan and white kid gloves.

quotes.quote: Oh my dear paws! Oh my fur and whiskers!
a bright brass plate with the name "W. RABBIT," engraved upon it
a fan and two or three pairs of tiny white kid gloves

payload.name: Mary Ann
payload.note: The Rabbit's housemaid, only named and never seen on stage; Alice is mistaken for her, so she is distinct from Alice herself.

payload.name: Pat
payload.note: The Rabbit's gardener, an Irishman (speaks with an Irish dialect) who is outside the window and handles the arm; he is heard but not seen.

stages.label: Pat
stages.text: Pat: an adult Irish gardener, a working man of middle age with a weathered build, ruddy skin, short hair and a clean-shaven face, dressed in a rough cotton shirt, waistcoat and corduroy trousers with a flat cap, in earthy browns and faded blues. He carries a spade as his only prop.

quotes.quote: Sure then I’m here! Digging for apples, yer honour!
Sure, it’s an arm, yer honour!

payload.name: Bill the Lizard
payload.note: The lizard Bill, sent down the chimney by the Rabbit's servants, kicked out by Alice, then later a juror at the trial who squeaks a pencil and cannot spell stupid; all three entries are the same lizard.

stages.label: Bill the Lizard
stages.text: Bill the Lizard: a small, feeble lizard of modest size, with a long tail, green-scaled and soft-bellied, standing upright on two legs in human posture. Dressed as a Victorian juror in a dark tailcoat, waistcoat and small white cravat, with a slate and pencil. Large, mournful eyes; a thin, wide-mouthed face with a slightly open mouth; small clawed hands; a patient, bewildered demeanour.

quotes.quote: a little feeble, squeaking voice
The poor little Lizard, Bill, was in the middle, being held up by two guinea-pigs
the poor little thing was waving its tail about in a melancholy way
One of the jurors had a pencil that squeaked.

payload.name: the guinea-pigs
payload.note: The two guinea-pigs who hold up Bill outside the house and rush at Alice; the same pair later cheering in court and being bagged, so both entries join this cluster and are distinguished only by section.

stages.label: the guinea-pigs
stages.text: the guinea-pigs: a pair of plump, short-eared guinea-pigs drawn as small animals with human posture and dress, standing upright; age: adult; build: round and compact; coat: soft short fur in warm brown and cream patches; facial notes: small dark eyes, rounded snout, whiskers; signature outfit: small period waistcoats and neckcloths in muted green and brown; signature props: a small brown glass bottle carried by one of them.

quotes.quote: being held up by two guinea-pigs, who were giving it something out of a bottle
Here one of the guinea-pigs cheered, and was immediately suppressed by the officers of the court.

payload.name: the puppy
payload.note: A large puppy in the wood that Alice plays with using a stick.

stages.label: the puppy
stages.text: the puppy: an enormous young dog, far larger than Alice, with a sturdy, rounded body on four legs, a broad head, large round eyes, short soft fur in a warm brown and cream coat, floppy ears and a thick tail. Animal form, not human-dressed. Set in a Victorian dream wood beside thistles and buttercups.

quotes.quote: An enormous puppy was looking down at her with large round eyes
till at last it sat down a good way off, panting, with its tongue hanging out of its mouth

payload.name: the Caterpillar
payload.note: The blue hookah-smoking Caterpillar on the mushroom in Wonderland, who questions Alice and gives her advice on the two sides of the mushroom; both entries describe this same individual across divisions.

stages.label: the Caterpillar
stages.text: the Caterpillar: a large blue caterpillar about three inches high, with a segmented, worm-like body, many small legs and folded human-like arms, wearing a simple period waistcoat and a small hat, holding a long hookah pipe. Blue body; its face is calm, heavy-lidded and sleepy.

quotes.quote: a large blue caterpillar, that was sitting on the top with its arms folded, quietly smoking a long hookah
it was exactly three inches high

payload.name: the White Rabbit's house
payload.note: A neat little house with a brass plate on the door; Alice grows inside its tidy room, with the stairs and window.)

stages.label: The White Rabbit's House
stages.text: The White Rabbit's house: a neat little Victorian cottage with a bright brass plate engraved 'W. RABBIT' on its front door. Inside, a tidy small room with a table set in the window, a looking-glass on the wall, and a narrow stairway; a chimney rises from the roof and a window with glass panes looks onto a garden with a cucumber-frame. Modest, orderly and cramped, with cottage brick and a slate roof.

quotes.quote: a neat little house, on the door of which was a bright brass plate with the name "W. RABBIT,"
a tidy little room with a table in the window
a little bottle that stood near the looking-glass
put one arm out of the window, and one foot up the chimney
a crash of broken glass

payload.name: the Rabbit's garden
payload.note: The area outside the Rabbit's house where Pat, Bill and the crowd of animals gather around the window and chimney.

stages.label: the Rabbit's garden
stages.text: the Rabbit's garden: a small cottage garden outside a low house with a window and a tall brick chimney, its roof of slate with a loose tile, cucumber-frames of glass panes set in the soil, bordered by a hedge, with a thick wood of trees visible beyond the garden wall, grass and cottage-garden plants, scattered broken glass and fallen pebbles, under a Victorian English countryside sky.

quotes.quote: a crash of broken glass, from which she concluded that it was just possible it had fallen into a cucumber-frame
Will the roof bear?—Mind that loose slate
she ran out of the house, and found quite a crowd of little animals and birds waiting outside

payload.name: The thick wood (where Alice meets the puppy and finds the mushroom)
payload.note: The wood Alice wanders into after escaping the crowd; distinguished from other woods by her meeting the puppy and finding the mushroom there.

stages.label: The thick wood
stages.text: The thick wood: a dense woodland of tall trees crowding close together, with thistles and buttercups growing among grass at ground level. A large mushroom stands near the path, about as tall as Alice, its broad cap rising above the grass. Dappled Victorian-era woodland light filters through the leaves, with no people in view.

quotes.quote: as she wandered about in the wood
while she was peering about anxiously among the trees
Alice dodged behind a great thistle
she leant against a buttercup to rest herself
There was a large mushroom growing near her, about the same height as herself

payload.name: the Pigeon
payload.note: An anxious mother Pigeon in a tree nest who mistakes Alice's long neck for a serpent's and accuses her of hunting eggs.

stages.label: The Pigeon
stages.text: The Pigeon: a large mother pigeon, a bird of middle age with a full, round breast and ruffled grey-and-white feathers, its wings held close and its head pushed forward on a long neck. It is drawn as a bird with human posture and dress, wearing a small shawl about its shoulders and a plain bonnet pinned above its crest. Its eyes are wide and anxious, its beak sharp and slightly open. Its only prop is a small tree-nest it sits upon, woven of twigs and moss.

quotes.quote: “Serpent!” screamed the Pigeon.
I’ve tried the roots of trees, and I’ve tried banks, and I’ve tried hedges
I’ve seen a good many little girls in my time

payload.name: Father William
payload.note: The old man in Alice's recited poem who stands on his head and balances an eel; he speaks with his son, the young man, in the verses.

payload.name: the young man
payload.note: The son of Father William in Alice's recited poem, who questions his father; exists only within the poem's verses.

payload.name: The mushroom clearing
aliases: the open place in the wood
payload.note: The open clearing in the wood where the Caterpillar sits on a large round mushroom and where Alice later nibbles it; the only place described as an open clearing rather than woodland in general.

stages.label: The mushroom clearing
stages.text: The mushroom clearing: an open place in a dreamlike wood, carpeted with grass and long green leaves, with tall trees rising around its edge whose tops are seen from above. At its centre stands a large, perfectly round mushroom, broad enough for a figure to sit upon, with a fat cap and a pale stem. Beyond the open ground the wood thickens into tall trunks and hedges, and a small house about four feet high stands at the clearing's edge.

quotes.quote: as it was perfectly round, she found this a very difficult question
the tops of the trees under which she had been wandering
she came suddenly upon an open place, with a little house in it about four feet high

payload.name: the treetops
payload.note: The high tree where the Pigeon has its nest, among the trees under which Alice had been wandering.

stages.label: the treetops
stages.text: the treetops: the leafy crowns of tall trees in a dream-wood, dense with interlaced branches and foliage, rising high above the ground. The highest tree in the wood stands among them, its uppermost boughs holding a large pigeon's nest. Sunlit leaves and twisting branches, with no people present.

quotes.quote: the tops of the trees under which she had been wandering
just as I'd taken the highest tree in the wood

payload.name: the open place with the little house
aliases: the little house in the open place
payload.note: An open place with a small house about four feet high, which Alice approaches once she has shrunk to nine inches.

stages.label: the open place with the little house
stages.text: the open place with the little house: a clearing opening in the wood among tall trees, with rough grass and scattered mushroom patches underfoot. In its middle stands a small house about four feet high, built as a modest cottage with a low roof, a narrow door and small windows, of weathered wood or stone with a Victorian storybook charm. Trees and branches ring the clearing, and the surrounding wood is dense and shadowed.

quotes.quote: an open place, with a little house in it about four feet high

payload.name: Fish-Footman
payload.note: A footman, so called by Alice from his face, who delivers the Queen's invitation to the Duchess at the door and then sits staring at the sky; not the Frog-Footman.

stages.label: Fish-Footman
stages.text: Fish-Footman: a young adult male footman, slender build, pale skin, powdered white hair curled all over the head, a long fish-like face with large round staring eyes and a wide mouth. Signature outfit: a formal livery coat with brass buttons in deep green with cream facings, knee breeches, white stockings and buckled shoes. He carries a great letter, nearly as large as himself, tucked under one arm. Dressed as a Victorian-era servant in a dream Wonderland.

quotes.quote: a footman in livery came running out of the wood
judging by his face only, she would have called him a fish
both footmen, Alice noticed, had powdered hair that curled all over their heads
The Fish-Footman began by producing from under his arm a great letter

payload.name: Frog-Footman
aliases: the footman with a round face and frog-like eyes
payload.note: The footman with a round face and large eyes who opens the door and repeats the invitation message; sits on the ground outside afterward.

stages.label: Frog-Footman
stages.text: Frog-Footman: an adult footman with a round face and large, bulging frog-like eyes, slim-to-average build, pale skin, powdered white hair curling all over the head, and a livery of a dark coat with brass buttons, a waistcoat, knee breeches, white stockings and buckled shoes. He carries no props of his own.

quotes.quote: another footman in livery, with a round face, and large eyes like a frog
both footmen, Alice noticed, had powdered hair that curled all over their heads

payload.name: The Duchess (kitchen, lullaby, croquet with the Queen)
payload.note: The short-tempered noblewoman in the smoky kitchen who nurses a baby and sings a violent lullaby, then leaves to play croquet with the Queen; distinguished from the moralising Duchess who walks with Alice by her kitchen and lullaby scenes.

stages.label: The Duchess
stages.text: The Duchess: a middle-aged noblewoman with a sharp, heavy-jawed face and a harsh, hoarse manner, in a rich but careless Victorian gown of deep plum silk with a lace collar, its hem smudged with soot. Her hair is pinned up in untidy grey-brown coils under a crooked lace cap. She is thin and angular, with long, bony hands, and carries a baby swaddled in a shawl. She is slightly stooped and unkempt, the image of ill temper.

quotes.quote: the Duchess was sitting on a three-legged stool in the middle, nursing a baby
singing a sort of lullaby to it as she did so, and giving it a violent shake at the end of every line

payload.name: Cook
payload.note: The Duchess's kitchen cook with a pepper-box, who stirs soup and is questioned about tarts; both entries describe the same cook in the Duchess's kitchen.

stages.label: Cook
stages.text: Cook: a stout, broad-shouldered Victorian kitchen cook of middle years, with a heavy, flushed face, hair tucked under a plain white cap, and sleeves rolled to the elbow. She wears a long dark-blue working dress under a coarse white apron, with a grey shawl at the shoulders. She carries a pepper-box in one hand, and a long iron ladle at the fire.

quotes.quote: the cook was leaning over the fire, stirring a large cauldron which seemed to be full of soup
She carried the pepper-box in her hand

payload.name: Baby
payload.note: The Duchess's infant, sneezing and howling, which Alice carries outside and which turns into a pig, then runs off into the wood.

stages.label: Baby
stages.text: Baby: a very young infant, newborn to toddling in age, small and plump with a queer, sprawling shape, limbs flung out in all directions. Skin pale and flushed from sneezing. Hair sparse or absent. Face with a very turn-up, snout-like nose and unusually small eyes. Wears a simple, loose white infant's gown or swaddling, with no other accessories. No props; carried by Alice.

quotes.quote: it was a queer-shaped little creature, and held out its arms and legs in all directions
its eyes were getting extremely small for a baby

payload.name: Cheshire Cat
payload.note: The grinning cat in the kitchen and trees who talks with Alice about the Hatter and the March Hare, and vanishes and reappears; the same grinning cat whose head appears in the air in the croquet-ground scene.

stages.label: Cheshire Cat
stages.text: Cheshire Cat: a large striped cat with a wide, broad grin from ear to ear, long claws and many teeth, drawn as an animal with a sitting posture and a human-like Victorian sense of humour. Its body is often absent, leaving only the grin hanging in the air, which fades slowly from the tail end first. Its coat is a soft striped tabby in grey and cream, with a bright pink tongue visible in the grin. It wears no clothing and carries no props.

quotes.quote: a large cat which was sitting on the hearth and grinning from ear to ear
it vanished quite slowly, beginning with the end of the tail, and ending with the grin
a curious appearance in the air: it puzzled her very much at first, but, after watching it a minute or two, she made it out to be a grin

payload.name: March Hare
payload.note: The mad anthropomorphic hare of the Mad Tea-Party, one of the three hosts, who offers wine, takes part in the riddles and story-telling, and appears in the Mad Tea-Party division as well as the court scene; the same individual as the March Hare at the tea party. Distinguish from the court-scene and house-scene entries only by identity, since all describe the same hare.

stages.label: March Hare
stages.text: March Hare: an anthropomorphic hare standing upright with human posture and dress, long upright ears, brown-and-tawny fur, adult in age, lean and slightly hunched build, a long muzzle with whiskers, round wide-set eyes, a wild restless look. He wears a rumpled period waistcoat, shirt and tailcoat in muted brown and cream, with a loose cravat and a tall hat tilted askew. He carries a teacup or teapot as his signature prop.

quotes.quote: the chimneys were shaped like ears and the roof was thatched with fur
the March Hare and the Hatter were having tea at it
It was the _best_ butter,” the March Hare meekly replied.
“Fifteenth,” said the March Hare.

payload.name: Hatter
payload.note: The Mad Hatter of the tea-party and the nervous first witness at the trial are the same individual; the pig-and-pepper mention is the same hatter named only in passing, so all three keys join one cluster.

stages.label: Hatter
stages.text: Hatter: an adult Victorian man of middle years, lean and slightly stooped, with untidy hair in need of cutting and a long pale face. He wears a shabby period waistcoat and frock coat with a tall, battered hat that is sometimes not his own. Colours are faded browns and greys with a dingy cravat. He carries a teacup and a slice of bread-and-butter, and an old pocket watch.

quotes.quote: Your hair wants cutting
He came in with a teacup in one hand and a piece of bread-and-butter in the other.
he had taken his watch out of his pocket

payload.name: The Queen (croquet invitation)
payload.note: A separate Queen who only sends the croquet invitation to the Duchess, mentioned in passing with no described traits tying her to the Queen of Hearts.

payload.name: Duchess's House
payload.note: A house standing in a wood, with a door opening into a smoky kitchen where the Duchess and cook are.Alice enters the kitchen here.

stages.label: Duchess's House
stages.text: Duchess's House: a house standing at the edge of a wood, its exterior plain and cottage-like with a door opening directly into one large kitchen. Inside, the kitchen is thick with smoke, with a great hearth and fire, a large cauldron, a three-legged stool, and pots, pans and plates scattered about. No people or animals are shown in this location entry.

quotes.quote: a footman in livery came running out of the wood
The door led right into a large kitchen, which was full of smoke from one end to the other
the cook was leaning over the fire, stirring a large cauldron

payload.name: The Duchess's wood
payload.note: The woods around the Duchess's house, where the footmen run out, the pig escapes and the Cat sits in a tree; set near the Duchess's residence, not the mushroom wood.

stages.label: The Duchess's wood
stages.text: The Duchess's wood: a dense woodland of tall shady trees set around the Duchess's house, with a clearing before its front door, broad trunks, low boughs where a cat might sit, and leafy undergrowth under a green canopy; the house stands at the wood's edge and the trees are the place where a footman runs out and a small pig trots away.

quotes.quote: a footman in livery came running out of the wood
she had to run back into the wood for fear of their hearing her
broke to pieces against one of the trees behind him
trot away quietly into the wood

payload.name: March Hare's House
payload.note: A large house with ear-shaped chimneys and a fur-thatched roof, where the March Hare is said to live; Alice approaches it at the end.

stages.label: March Hare's House
stages.text: March Hare's House: a very large house in a Wonderland wood, its chimneys shaped like ears and its roof thatched with fur. Tall trees and tangled undergrowth surround it, with a clearing of worn ground before the front. No people are present; the house stands alone among the trees and mushrooms of the wood.

quotes.quote: the chimneys were shaped like ears and the roof was thatched with fur
It was so large a house

payload.name: the Dormouse
payload.note: The sleepy dormouse at the Mad Tea-Party between the Hare and the Hatter, who tells the treacle-well story; the same Dormouse appears in the trial chapter, so both entries are one cluster.

stages.label: the Dormouse
stages.text: the Dormouse: a small, drowsy talking dormouse, grey-brown fur with a pale belly, round ears, a thin tail and small whiskers, standing and sitting upright in human posture. Age: adult. Build: slight and plump. Skin: grey-brown fur. Face: small dark eyes that are often shut, a pink nose, long whiskers. Signature outfit: a faded blue waistcoat with a small brass button and a dull green neckcloth. Signature prop: a china teacup held in its small paws.

quotes.quote: a Dormouse was sitting between them, fast asleep
he poured a little hot tea upon its nose
I wish you wouldn’t squeeze so

payload.name: Queen of Hearts
payload.note: The short-tempered Queen of Hearts who orders executions, runs the croquet game, sits on the throne at the trial, and appears across the divisions; the one ruler named Queen of Hearts with the Knave's trial and croquet-ground.

stages.label: Queen of Hearts
stages.text: Queen of Hearts: a flat, oblong playing-card royal with a head, arms and legs, drawn as an imperious adult woman of middle age with a commanding bearing. Her hair is dark and bound under a small golden crown. Her skin is fair. Her signature outfit is a long crimson velvet gown with a wide golden-edged collar, trimmed with heart motifs, in deep red and gold. Her signature prop is a rounded golden sceptre held in one hand.

quotes.quote: The Queen turned crimson with fury
ornamented all over with diamonds
the balls were live hedgehogs, the mallets live flamingoes
frowning like a thunderstorm

payload.name: Time
payload.note: Personified Time, with whom the Hatter has quarrelled; mentioned only and never present on stage.

payload.name: Elsie
payload.note: One of the three little sisters in the Dormouse's story, who lived at the bottom of a treacle-well; told of, not present.

payload.name: Lacie
payload.note: One of the three little sisters in the Dormouse's story, living in the treacle-well; told of, not present.

payload.name: Tillie
payload.note: One of the three little sisters in the Dormouse's story, living in the treacle-well; told of, not present.

payload.name: Tea-table under a tree
aliases: the table in front of the house
payload.note: A large table set out under a tree in front of a house, where the tea-party takes place.

stages.label: Tea-table under a tree
stages.text: Tea-table under a tree: a large wooden table set out in the open under a spreading tree, in front of a house, with a cloth laid across it and many tea-things and cups scattered over its surface. The tree shades the table, with leafy branches and a rough trunk. The house stands behind it with a plain, old-fashioned Victorian front. Ground is level grass before the table.

quotes.quote: There was a table set out under a tree in front of the house
The table was a large one, but the three were all crowded together at one corner of it
there was nothing on it but tea

payload.name: The wood beyond the tea-party
payload.note: The wood Alice picks her way through after leaving the Mad Tea-Party, on her way to the garden; identified by its link to the tea-party and the tree-door.

stages.label: The wood beyond the tea-party
stages.text: The wood beyond the tea-party: a dense, dreamlike Victorian woodland of tangled undergrowth and close-set trees with twisted, sunlit trunks and drifting leaves, the path threading between them over uneven, mossy ground. One tall, broad tree stands apart with a small ordinary wooden door set into its trunk, its frame and hinges plain and old. Ferns, toadstools and bramble tangles crowd the edges of the path, and the wood opens gently toward the bright garden beyond.

quotes.quote: as she picked her way through the wood
one of the trees had a door leading right into it

payload.name: The beautiful garden
payload.note: The bright, fountain-cooled garden reached through the tree-door at the end of the tea-party division; the destination beyond the garden door.

stages.label: The beautiful garden
stages.text: The beautiful garden: a bright Wonderland garden of level lawns and raised flower-beds in vivid colours, with cool fountains splashing among them. Clipped hedges and tall trees frame the grounds, and a small low passage of pale stone and dark wood leads in from the tree-door set into a great trunk. Paths of pale gravel wind between beds and fountains under a clear, open sky.

quotes.quote: she found herself at last in the beautiful garden, among the bright flower-beds and the cool fountains.
a door leading right into it

payload.name: Two
payload.note: One of the three card gardeners painting roses red; he explains the mistake to Alice, and is a playing card rather than a human in units 1-11 and 25. Distinguished from Five and Seven by his role as the spokesman who explains to Alice.

stages.label: Two, card gardener
stages.text: Two: a flat, oblong playing-card gardener of the Queen's pack, with a head, arms and legs at the corners of the card, drawn with the same pattern on his back as the rest of the pack. Adult in age, humble and anxious in bearing, wearing the plain card gardener's garb of the pack with a paintbrush in hand and red paint on his fingers. Painting the white roses of the rose-tree red.

quotes.quote: there were three gardeners at it, busily painting them red
these were all shaped like the three gardeners, oblong and flat, with their hands and feet at the corners
the pattern on their backs was the same as the rest of the pack

payload.name: Five
payload.note: One of the three card gardeners painting roses; he blames Seven for splashing paint and warns the others of the Queen's approach. Distinguished from Two and Seven by blaming Seven and giving the warning.

stages.label: Five, card gardener
stages.text: Five: a flat, oblong playing card gardener with a head, arms and legs at the corners, body of a Victorian card courtier, pattern of spades on the back, holding a paintbrush and dressed in a plain card-gardener's tunic in red and white, a flat card figure with hands and feet at the corners, standing among white roses being painted red, with a sulky, aggrieved bearing.

quotes.quote: there were three gardeners at it, busily painting them red
"I couldn't help it," said Five, in a sulky tone; "Seven jogged my elbow."
these were all shaped like the three gardeners, oblong and flat, with their hands and feet at the corners

payload.name: Seven
payload.note: One of the three card gardeners painting roses; he is blamed by Five and is the one who checks himself when he sees Alice. Distinguished from Two and Five by being the one blamed for the splashing.

stages.label: Seven, card gardener
stages.text: Seven: a flat, oblong playing-card gardener with a head, arms and legs at the corners of his card body, with a plain card pattern on his back. Age: young adult. Build: slim and flat as a card. Skin: pale, fair. Hair: short, neatly cropped dark hair. Facial notes: a sharp, somewhat indignant face. Outfit: a plain gardener's apron over a Victorian-style waistcoat and trousers in muted green, with a small cap. Props: a paintbrush in one hand and a small pot of red paint.

quotes.quote: there were three gardeners at it, busily painting them red
these were all shaped like the three gardeners, oblong and flat, with their hands and feet at the corners
Seven flung down his brush

payload.name: King of Hearts
payload.note: The mild, timid King who walks in the procession, quietly pardons the condemned players and sits as judge at the trial; distinguished from the Queen by his timidity and pardons.

stages.label: King of Hearts
stages.text: King of Hearts: an elderly, mild, timid man of about sixty with a short grey-white beard and mild anxious face, wearing a tall gold crown set over a great white judge's wig, round spectacles, and a long crimson royal robe with ermine trim over a white waistcoat and knee breeches. Flat oblong playing-card body with head, arms and legs at the corners, decorated with red hearts. Carries a small sceptre in one gloved hand.

quotes.quote: That's the judge, she said to herself, because of his great wig.
as he wore his crown over the wig, (look at the frontispiece if you want to see how he did it,) he did not look at all comfortable
the King put on his spectacles and looked anxiously round
these were ornamented all over with diamonds

payload.name: the Knave of Hearts
payload.note: The Knave of Hearts, a playing card who carries the King's crown in the procession and is later tried for stealing the tarts; the same individual across all three entries, shown carrying the crown, standing accused in chains, and as the cardboard card figure on trial in Alice's dream.

stages.label: the Knave of Hearts
stages.text: the Knave of Hearts: an oblong, flat playing card made of cardboard, with head, arms and legs at the corners, a heart suit ornament on its front, and a plain card-stock finish. Age appears youthful; build slight and flat; skin pale card-white; hair a dark painted brown; face simple, with a bowed, smiling expression. Signature outfit: a red and crimson tunic with a white collar and red breeches. Signature prop: a crimson velvet cushion carrying the King's crown.

quotes.quote: Then followed the Knave of Hearts, carrying the King's crown on a crimson velvet cushion
the Knave was standing before them, in chains, with a soldier on each side to guard him
being made entirely of cardboard

payload.name: the White Rabbit
payload.note: The single anxious White Rabbit of Wonderland who whispers the Duchess's sentence in the croquet procession and later acts as herald of the court, blowing the trumpet, reading the accusation and calling witnesses; all three entries are the same rabbit across divisions.

stages.label: White Rabbit
stages.text: The White Rabbit: an anxious white rabbit standing upright with human posture, white fur, pink eyes, and long ears, dressed in a waistcoat with a pocket watch. Hurried and nervous in manner, he carries a brass trumpet in one hand and a rolled parchment scroll in the other, and wears round spectacles when reading. Flat, fragile, and precise in his gestures, with a small shrill voice.

quotes.quote: Alice recognised the White Rabbit: it was talking in a hurried nervous manner
near the King was the White Rabbit, with a trumpet in one hand, and a scroll of parchment in the other
The White Rabbit put on his spectacles.

payload.name: the playing-card soldiers
payload.note: The ten oblong card soldiers with clubs who march in the royal procession, form the croquet arches and carry out the Queen's orders in the croquet-ground scenes.

stages.label: the playing-card soldiers
stages.text: the playing-card soldiers: ten flat, oblong card soldiers of the Queen's pack, each with a head, arms and legs at the corners of the card body, carrying a club. Their faces are simple and painted, with stiff moustaches and small pointed hats, dressed in the pack's patterned livery in red and black. Their build is slender and uniform, all identical in size and shape.

quotes.quote: First came ten soldiers carrying clubs; these were all shaped like the three gardeners, oblong and flat, with their hands and feet at the corners
the soldiers had to double themselves up and to stand on their hands and feet, to make the arches

payload.name: the courtiers
payload.note: Ten diamond-decorated card courtiers who walk two by two in the procession.

stages.label: The ten courtiers
stages.text: the courtiers: ten flat, oblong playing-card courtiers, each with a head, arms and legs at the corners of a card-shaped body, the whole front ornamented all over with red and black diamonds. Each card bears a simple card-face head and small hands and feet, drawn as a courtly figure. Their dress is a period courtly suit in the same card pattern, with a stiff collar and a short cloak, in red and white, with a diamond motif. Each walks upright in pairs with a flat, card-like silhouette.

quotes.quote: these were ornamented all over with diamonds, and walked two and two, as the soldiers did
these were all shaped like the three gardeners, oblong and flat, with their hands and feet at the corners

payload.name: the royal children
payload.note: Ten heart-decorated children who skip hand in hand in the procession.

stages.label: The royal children
stages.text: The royal children: ten small children of the Queen's household, aged about five to nine, slim and quick-moving with rounded shoulders. Flat oblong card figures with heads, arms and legs at the corners, decorated all over with red hearts on their pattern. Hair short and neat, faces simple and cheerful. Each wears a plain pinafore-style tunic in red and white with a heart motif, and carries no props of their own.

quotes.quote: there were ten of them, and the little dears came jumping merrily along hand in hand, in couples: they were all ornamented with hearts

payload.name: the executioner
payload.note: The Queen's executioner who argues about beheading the Cat and runs to fetch the Duchess in unit 70.

stages.label: the executioner
stages.text: The executioner: a middle-aged man, lean and stooped, with a grizzled moustache and greying side-whiskers. He is drawn as a flat, oblong playing card with head, arms and legs. He wears a dark Victorian-era executioner's hood-less black coat with a high collar, a red sash, and a tall black top hat, and carries a long-handled axe held at his side. No gore or injury is shown.

quotes.quote: he had never had to do such a thing before, and he wasn’t going to begin at _his_ time of life
And the executioner went off like an arrow.

payload.name: The Duchess (imprisoned, to be executed)
payload.note: The Duchess sentenced to execution who is fetched by the executioner at the end; named only in mention, distinguished by her imprisonment and sentence rather than any on-page scene.

payload.name: the flamingo
payload.note: A live flamingo used as Alice's mallet; it twists its neck and at one point flies off into a tree.

stages.label: the flamingo
stages.text: the flamingo: a live flamingo with long pink-feathered body, slender long legs and a long curving neck, of a size that can be tucked under a girl's arm with its legs hanging down. Its neck is long, flexible and prone to twisting, its plumage pale rose-pink with darker wing edges, and its beak is long and bent downward. It is a bird, not a human, with no clothing or props.

quotes.quote: she succeeded in getting its body tucked away, comfortably enough, under her arm, with its legs hanging down
it _would_ twist itself round and look up in her face

payload.name: the hedgehogs
payload.note: Live hedgehogs used as croquet balls, which roll away and fight one another.

stages.label: the hedgehogs
stages.text: the hedgehogs: small live hedgehogs, each with a rounded body and a coat of brown and fawn spines, short legs, a pointed snout and small dark eyes; in the game they are used as croquet balls, so they are small, round and compact, able to curl into a ball and unroll to crawl away.

quotes.quote: the balls were live hedgehogs
the hedgehog had unrolled itself, and was in the act of crawling away

payload.name: Garden by the rose-tree
aliases: the garden entrance by the rose-tree
payload.note: The garden entrance near the rose-tree where the card gardeners paint the white rose red and Alice first meets them; a distinct spot from the beautiful garden and the garden door.

stages.label: Garden by the rose-tree
stages.text: Garden by the rose-tree: a garden entrance in a Victorian dream Wonderland, marked by one large rose-tree standing near the opening, its blooms white and freshly splashed with red paint. Neat garden beds and a low path lead inward, with clipped hedges and tidy flower-beds bordering the entrance. Tall trees rise beyond the garden walls, and a large flower-pot stands nearby. No people.

quotes.quote: A large rose-tree stood near the entrance of the garden
the roses growing on it were white
we put a white one in by mistake

payload.name: the Queen's croquet-ground
payload.note: The single walled garden croquet-ground of the Queen where the flamingo-and-hedgehog game is played and executions are ordered; both entries describe this same place, so they form one cluster.

stages.label: Queen's croquet-ground
stages.text: Queen's croquet-ground: an enclosed garden of uneven ridges and furrows over lawn, with a few tall trees at its far side and a tall walled border around it. Vegetation is lush green grass and shrubs, with trees behind the walls. Architecture is minimal: a low garden wall and a rounded hedge border, with small painted arches of doubled-up soldiers as hoops. Landmarks are the ridged ground, the scattered arches and the distant trees. Victorian dream-Wonderland setting; no people present.

quotes.quote: it was all ridges and furrows; the balls were live hedgehogs, the mallets live flamingoes
her flamingo was gone across to the other side of the garden, where Alice could see it trying in a helpless sort of way to fly up into a tree
by the end of half an hour or so there were no arches left

payload.name: The Duchess (arm in arm with Alice, moralising)
payload.note: The ugly, sharp-chinned, moralising Duchess who walks arm in arm with Alice and is driven off by the Queen's arrival; the same Duchess met earlier in the kitchen, so her kitchen scene is a separate cluster only where its notes point to a different portrayal.

stages.label: The Duchess
stages.text: The Duchess: a very ugly older woman with a sharp, pointed chin, short enough to rest it on a girl's shoulder. Thin, stooped build, pale sallow skin, grey-streaked hair pinned under a large, untidy hat. Sharp, pinched features and a sour, scheming expression. Signature outfit: a faded plum-coloured Victorian gown with a lace collar and a dusty shawl. Carries no props of her own.

quotes.quote: the Duchess was _very_ ugly
exactly the right height to rest her chin upon Alice’s shoulder, and it was an uncomfortably sharp chin

payload.name: the Gryphon
payload.note: The Gryphon of the Mock Turtle's story and the Lobster Quadrille: a winged creature with an eagle's head and lion's body who guides Alice, interrupts the Mock Turtle, and hurries her to the trial; the same individual as the Gryphon who whispers in the court.

stages.label: the Gryphon
stages.text: The Gryphon: a winged creature with an eagle's head and a lion's body, with wings folded at its back and forepaws. It is a fantastical beast of the Wonderland tradition, drawn in the Victorian illustrated manner of the book, with an eagle's beak and a lion's tawny-gold coat. Its feathers are warm brown and cream, and its wings are large and dark-tipped. No clothing, no props.

quotes.quote: a Gryphon, lying fast asleep in the sun

payload.name: the Mock Turtle
payload.note: Sorrowful calf-headed creature with a turtle's tail who tells of his schooldays in the sea (The Mock Turtle's Story); the same creature who later describes the Lobster Quadrille and sings Beautiful Soup, so both entries belong to this cluster.

stages.label: The Mock Turtle
stages.text: The Mock Turtle: a sorrowful, sobbing sea creature with a calf's head and a turtle's tail, whose body is that of a turtle with a shell and flat flapper-like forelimbs. Its eyes are large and full of tears, and it is stiff and heavy in build, with a deep hollow voice. Its colouring is pale and watery, with a dull grey-green shell, a soft cream underside and a mournful look.

quotes.quote: Once," said the Mock Turtle at last, with a deep sigh, "I was a real Turtle."
The Mock Turtle sighed deeply, and drew the back of one flapper across his eyes.
sitting sad and lonely on a little ledge of rock

payload.name: the old Turtle master (Tortoise)
payload.note: The old Turtle who taught the Mock Turtle at school under the sea; only recalled in the Mock Turtle's story, not present on stage.

payload.name: the Drawling-master (old conger-eel)
payload.note: The old conger-eel who came once a week to teach Drawling, Stretching and Fainting in Coils; recalled in the Mock Turtle's story only.

payload.name: the Classics master (old crab)
payload.note: The old crab who taught the Gryphon the Classics, recalled only in The Mock Turtle's Story and not present; a different crab from the mother crab, distinguished by her role as a schoolmaster.

payload.name: the rock ledge by the sea
payload.note: The lonely rock ledge where the Mock Turtle sits sobbing and tells his story, near the sea.

stages.label: the rock ledge by the sea
stages.text: the rock ledge by the sea: a small, bare shelf of grey rock jutting over the water at the edge of the shore, with weathered stone surfaces, sparse tufts of sea-grass and salt-stained crevices, the open sea stretching flat and pale beyond it, no buildings in sight.

quotes.quote: sitting sad and lonely on a little ledge of rock

payload.name: the undersea school
payload.note: The school under the sea attended by the Mock Turtle in his youth, existing only in his recollection; not shown on stage.

stages.label: The undersea school
stages.text: The undersea school: a schoolhouse on the sea floor, its rooms lit by filtered green-blue water, with coral walls, drifting sea-grass and kelp, sand-dusted stone steps and sunken arched windows. Rocky outcrops and shell-strewn sand surround it, and it has no people.

quotes.quote: we went to school in the sea
living at the bottom of the sea

payload.name: Whiting
payload.note: A sea fish addressed in the Mock Turtle's song; it urges a snail to join the dance. Described as the subject of the song, not a physical presence on stage.

payload.name: Snail
payload.note: A snail in the Mock Turtle's song who refuses the whiting's invitation to join the dance, saying 'Too far, too far!'.

payload.name: Porpoise
payload.note: A porpoise in the song who treads on the whiting's tail; mentioned in the whiting's explanation and in the Mock Turtle's remark about fish needing a porpoise.

payload.name: Lobsters
payload.note: Sea creatures who serve as partners in the Lobster Quadrille; they are thrown out to sea and sing of their dance in the song.

payload.name: Sea-shore
payload.note: The undersea setting where the Lobster Quadrille would be danced along the shore and where the whiting and lobsters are placed.

stages.label: Sea-shore
stages.text: Sea-shore: a wide strip of pale shingle and sand running along the edge of a calm undersea sea, with the open water beyond it, scattered with drifting jelly-fish. Smooth rounded stones, clumps of seaweed and coral outcrops line the shore, and the water fades to deep green-blue further out.

quotes.quote: you first form into a line along the sea-shore
They are waiting on the shingle—will you come and join the dance?
when you’ve cleared all the jelly-fish out of the way
as far out to sea as you can

payload.name: The Queen of Hearts' court of justice
aliases: the court of the Queen of Hearts
payload.note: The single courtroom of the Queen of Hearts where the trial of the Knave takes place; the Lobster Quadrille entry, which only mentions the trial heard in the distance, is the same court and is distinguished only by being unseen on stage.

stages.label: The Queen of Hearts' court of justice
stages.text: The Queen of Hearts' court of justice: a large, crowded courtroom of tall, sombre stone walls and a high roof, with a raised royal throne for the King and Queen of Hearts at one end, a judge's great wig-marked bench, and a jury-box holding twelve jurors writing on slates. In the centre stands a long table bearing a large dish of tarts, and the floor is strewn with a crowd of little birds, beasts and flat playing-card courtiers. Doors lead off to the side, scattered papers litter the floor, and the space is formal and dim.

quotes.quote: the King and Queen of Hearts were seated on their throne
In the very middle of the court was a table, with a large dish of tarts upon it
she jumped up in such a hurry that she tipped over the jury-box
The twelve jurors were all writing very busily on slates.

payload.name: the jury
payload.note: The twelve jurors, birds and beasts who write on slates and act together as one body in the court; same jury in both the tart trial and Alice's trial, so the two entries are one cluster.

stages.label: the jury
stages.text: the jury: twelve creatures, a mix of animals and birds, each drawn as an animal or bird with human posture and period dress such as waistcoats and hats; they sit in the jury-box, each holding a slate and pencil. Their forms vary, including a lizard among them. Flat card-like jury members are not used; they are animal and bird figures.

quotes.quote: those twelve creatures, (she was obliged to say "creatures," you see, because some of them were animals, and some were birds,)
The twelve jurors were all writing very busily on slates.
the poor little juror (it was Bill, the Lizard)

payload.name: the officers of the court
payload.note: The court officers who suppress the guinea-pigs, remove the Dormouse and attend the Queen's orders in the Hatter's evidence and cook scenes; distinct from the card soldiers who march in the procession.

stages.label: officers of the court
stages.text: the officers of the court: a group of typical members, adult men of middle age, lean and upright, with a stern, dutiful bearing; clean-shaven or with short side whiskers, pale complexion, neat dark hair under a plain low-crowned hat. Each wears a dark formal court coat with high collar over a white shirt and waistcoat, with a brass-buttoned tabard of the Queen's livery in red and gold. They carry a large canvas bag tied with strings and a folded list or scroll.

quotes.quote: They had a large canvas bag, which tied up at the mouth with strings
Bring me the list of the singers in the last concert!

payload.name: the pack of cards
payload.note: The playing cards of the court who rise up and fly at Alice at the end of the dream; distinct from the jury of birds and beasts.

stages.label: the pack of cards
stages.text: the pack of cards: a group of flat, oblong playing cards of the Queen's court, each card a cardboard figure with a head, arms and legs, painted in the suits of hearts, spades, diamonds and clubs with court-card faces and rich period colours of red, black and gold trim, with plain card backs showing at the edges as they rise.

quotes.quote: being made entirely of cardboard
You’re nothing but a pack of cards!
the whole pack rose up into the air, and came flying down upon her
